transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/time: 2025-06-18 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Meeting id: ff-20250618-verdant-001
Attendees: Maria Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood CSM), Andre Lopez (Redwood SE), Priya Raman (Verdant VP Product), Liam O'Neal (Verdant Head of ML Ops), Sofia Martinez (Verdant Security Lead), Noah Chen (Verdant Data Engineer)

Summary:
- Kickoff for Verdant Analytics onboarding to Redwood Inference. Goals: access setup, security alignment, initial performance benchmarks, pilot scoping and timeline.
- Primary concerns: SSO/SAML, VPC/private deployment options, KMS/encryption, and predictable latency for inference at 95th pct.
- Agreed immediate next steps: runbench plan, send runbook, schedule security deep-dive.

Topics covered: onboarding checklist, environment access, network options (hosted vs private), security and compliance (SOC2/KMS/audit logs), pilot workload and success metrics, benchmark plan, rollouts and canary policies, support/ES escalation path.

-- Transcript (auto-generated, medium quality, some mis-recognitions) --
[00:00] Maria Chen: All right everyone, um hi — thanks for joining. This is Maria from Redwood, I'll kick us off, quick intros then we'll go through the onboarding playbook and the bench plan.
[00:32] Priya Raman: Hi Maria, Priya here, thanks for setting this up. We have a bunch of folks on my side tuned in because we want to get this pilot moving quickly.
[00:45] Jordan Patel: Jordan (CSM) from Redwood, I'll be coordinating post-kickoff and helping with the runbook tasks.
[01:05] Liam O'Neal: Liam, ML Ops. We're primarily concerned about throughput at peak and how the KV cache works with our streaming use case.
[01:22] Andre Lopez: Andre (SE). I'll own the benchmark and the initial integration pieces — hello everyone.
[01:35] Sofia Martinez: Sofia, security. I'll be leading the SOC2/KMS discussions and need to know how logs are stored/audited.
[01:48] Noah Chen: Noah, data engineering — I'll handle credentials and sample data.
[02:05] Maria Chen: Great, quick agenda: 1) access & roles, 2) network deployment options, 3) security & compliance, 4) benchmark/pilot scope and timelines, 5) wrap up and action items. Sound good?
[02:28] Priya Raman: Yep. Also timeline: we were hoping for a pilot in July, production by Sept if all goes well.
[02:40] Maria Chen: That's reasonable, we'll map the tasks.
[03:05] Jordan Patel: Two housekeeping notes: we'll share the onboarding runbook right after this call and a calendar for the deep dives. Also we'll add the shared deck link in the thread.
[03:20] Maria Chen: quick note on access: we support two patterns — hosted with private network peering / dedicated pools, or Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem). For the pilot, most customers start on hosted with VPC peering. Does Verdant have constraints that push to private immediately?
[03:50] Sofia Martinez: For PHI-ish data we might need private or at least strict residency. We are still scoping as we have clients in EU and US — data residency matters.
[04:08] Noah Chen: The pilot data is synthetic but production will include some EU-resident customers. We need to ensure model inference doesn't leave region.
[04:20] Andre Lopez: Ok, good to know. For the pilot we can do hosted in the EU region and enable KMS. If you need fully private control plane we can scope Redwood Private, but that adds onboarding time.
[04:42] Liam O'Neal: Can you remind us what's the difference in latency/cost between hosted and dedicated? We need to quantify.
[04:56] Maria Chen: Sure — hosted is quickest to start, multi-tenant but with isolation at the tenant layer; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools so more predictable tail latency and throughput, typically 10-30% cost delta depending on utilization, but we can run a cost model with your traffic.
[05:20] Priya Raman: Sounds good. Our success metric for pilot is p95 latency under 350ms for 4k token sequences at baseline traffic. Is that realistic?
[05:34] Andre Lopez: 4k tokens and 350ms p95 is challenging on CPU, but on modern GPU setups and with KV cache/prefix caching it's doable if we tune quantization and batching. We'll put together a realistic expectation in the benchmark plan.
[05:56] Maria Chen: We'll capture that as a KPI for the bench run.
[06:10] Jordan Patel: Security checklist: SSO, KMS, audit logs, SOC2 artifact review, and network diagram. We'll need the IdP metadata and the list of admin users.
[06:28] Sofia Martinez: We'll send SAML metadata, but we need to know what RBAC granularity Redwood supports — can we have team-level roles?
[06:40] Andre Lopez: Yes, RBAC supports org->team->role mapping; we'll share a sample role matrix in the runbook.
[06:52] Noah Chen: For keys: do you support customer-managed KMS? We prefer bring-your-own keys.
[07:05] Maria Chen: Yes, we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and HSM integrations for Private. For hosted we offer envelope encryption and you can provide a key for encryption at rest.
[07:20] Priya Raman: Any additional compliance docs we should expect?
[07:28] Jordan Patel: We'll share SOC2 Type II report (redacted) and our standard security whitepaper. Also an optional compliance questionnaire if you want deeper posture.
[07:42] Priya Raman: Great.
[08:00] Maria Chen: Moving to pilot scope: what workload are we testing? Priya?
[08:10] Priya Raman: We'll test two main flows: 1) interactive chat for customer support agents (short prompts, high concurrency), 2) document summarization (longer seq lengths, batch jobs). We want both to be representative.
[08:30] Andre Lopez: That's helpful; we'll ask for a sample payload distribution and token histograms. Noah, can you share sample traces?
[08:40] Noah Chen: Yes, I can export a 100k-sample trace with sequence length distribution tomorrow.
[08:50] Andre Lopez: Perfect — that'll drive batch sizes and kernel selection for the runtime.
[09:05] Maria Chen: For evaluation: we'll run quality checks as well as perf. Redwood Optimize can run prompt evals and compare model variants — want us to include a quality baseline?
[09:20] Priya Raman: Yes, we need quality baselines for our SLAs.
[09:30] Liam O'Neal: Also, what about model versions — can we pin a version and do canary rollouts?
[09:40] Andre Lopez: Absolutely. We support pinning and canary policies; you can route a percentage to the canary and monitor metrics, with automatic rollback rules if latency or quality regresses.
[09:58] Maria Chen: Great. Now a brief on the benchmark plan: Andre will run tests for: cold start, steady-state throughput, p95/p99 latency, and quantization tradeoffs. We'll test both hosted EU region and a Dedicated pool simulation.
[10:22] Andre Lopez: I'll set up a harness that replays your traces, instrument token-level latency, and capture cost per 1M tokens. Expect initial numbers within 7-10 business days after we get samples and credentials.
[10:40] Priya Raman: That timeline works.
[11:00] Sofia Martinez: On logs: we need audit logs retention for 12 months and exportability to our SIEM. Is that supported?
[11:12] Jordan Patel: Yes, logs can be exported to your S3 or pushed to a SIEM; retention settings are configurable for Dedicated and Private. For hosted we have standard retention but can add extended retention as an add-on.
[11:35] Noah Chen: Network-wise, do you require a particular peering setup? We prefer not to open wide egress if possible.
[11:46] Andre Lopez: For hosted VPC peering we can set up an interface VPC endpoint and restrict egress. For Private, you manage the network. We'll share the exact network requirements in the runbook.
[12:05] Priya Raman: About escalations: if we hit a production incident how does support work?
[12:14] Jordan Patel: We'll attach a CSM and a designated SE. For Dedicated/Private customers we include a 24/7 escalation path depending on SLA tier. We'll formalize in the contract.
[12:30] Maria Chen: Quick question from the team: are there recommended quantization profiles for transformer LLMs for better throughput without quality loss?
[12:43] Andre Lopez: Yes, we have preflight quantization recipes — 8-bit + selective FP16 for attention layers tends to keep top-line quality but reduces memory and improves batch sizes. We'll propose a profile in the bench report.
[13:05] Priya Raman: Do you have any pre-built connectors for our vector DB (we use an in-house store), or is it all via embeddings?
[13:18] Andre Lopez: We integrate at the API layer; embeddings are first-class and you can push to your vector DB. We don't require a specific DB. If you want hosted similarity search, Redwood can suggest patterns.
[13:35] Liam O'Neal: Ok. One more: rate limits. We need to know per-account QPS and burst characteristics.
[13:45] Maria Chen: Default rate limits depend on plan; we'll share current limits and you can request increases for the pilot. Dedicated removes shared throttles and you get guaranteed throughput.
[14:05] Priya Raman: Anything else around data residency — can we pin region for inference so 3rd party models' calls don't leave region?
[14:20] Andre Lopez: You can pin nodes to region and ensure model variants are cached in that region. For hosted, we replicate model weights only where allowed. We'll document guarantees and fallback behavior.
[14:40] Noah Chen: About the evals — do you support automated regression alerts if quality drops post-deploy?
[14:50] Jordan Patel: Yes, Redwood Optimize supports eval hooks, dataset-based checks, and alerts when a metric deviates. We'll tie those to the rollout policies if you want automatic rollback.
[15:10] Maria Chen: Ok moving to timeline mapping on-screen (shared deck link: https://app.redwood.ai/decks/onboarding/verdant-kickoff ) — high level: access & SSO by 6/20, sample traces by 6/19, bench runs 6/23-7/2, security deep-dive week of 6/30, pilot start early July.
[15:40] Priya Raman: Can we get a packaged checklist for legal/procurement too? We might need to coordinate with procurement for contract terms.
[15:52] Jordan Patel: Yes, we'll include a procurement checklist and our standard contract timelines.
[16:05] Sofia Martinez: A note on HIPAA — some of our customers may be covered; will Redwood sign a BAA?
[16:15] Maria Chen: We can discuss BAA for Private deployments. For hosted we have customers on BAAs under certain conditions; we'll bring legal into the security deep-dive.
[16:30] Liam O'Neal: For benchmark data, any anonymization guidelines? We might want to mask PII before sending traces.
[16:40] Andre Lopez: Masking is fine and recommended. Synthetic or anonymized traces work well; we just need representative token lengths and concurrency.
[16:55] Priya Raman: On pricing — at a high level what should we expect for pilot costs?
[17:05] Maria Chen: For pilot, expect usage-based billing for hosted; we can provide an estimate based on expected token volume. For Dedicated we'll provide a reserved capacity quote if you want to move that direction. We'll follow up with a simple cost model.
[17:25] Noah Chen: Please include cost per 1M tokens for the two workflows.
[17:32] Andre Lopez: We'll provide cost and latency tradeoff charts in the bench report.
[17:45] Maria Chen: Any blockers from the Verdant side to start?
[17:52] Priya Raman: We'll need the SAML metadata and a list of users; otherwise good to go.
[18:05] Noah Chen: I'll export and share the 100k-sample traces by end of day tomorrow.
[18:16] Sofia Martinez: I'll collate SOC2 scope and a preliminary compliance checklist.
[18:28] Maria Chen: Fantastic. Final quick recap: Maria will send runbook and deck; Andre will own bench harness; Jordan will coordinate schedule and procurement checklist; Verdant will send SAML metadata, sample traces, and SOC2 list.
[18:46] Jordan Patel: I'll drop the calendar invites for security deep-dive and bench kickoff.
[19:00] Priya Raman: Thanks everyone — excited to get started.
[19:10] Maria Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up with artifacts and next steps.

(Transcript ends — some names may be transcribed imperfectly.)
